questions.q: During the transition of electron from state A to state C of a Bohr atom, the wavelength of emitted radiation is $2000 Å$ and it becomes $6000 Å$ when the electron jumps from state B to state C. Then the wavelength of the radiation emitted during the transition of electrons from state A to state B is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\frac{h c}{\lambda_1}=E_0 z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_c^2}-\frac{1}{n_A^2}\right) ....(i) And \frac{h c}{\lambda_2}=$E_0 z² \left(\frac{1}{n_c^2}-\frac{1}{n_B^2}\right)$ So for $A$ and $B$ ....(ii) $\frac{h c}{\lambda_3}=E_0 z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_B^2}-\frac{1}{n_A^2}\right) Clearly subtracting equation (ii) from equation (i) \begin{aligned}$& h c\left[\frac{1}{\lambda_1}-\frac{1}{\lambda_2}\right]=$E_0 z²\left[\frac{1}{n_B^2}-\frac{1}{n_A^2}\right]=\frac{h c}{\lambda_3}$\\ & \Rightarrow $\frac{1}{\lambda_3}=\frac{1}{\lambda_1}-\frac{1}{\lambda_2} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda_3}=\frac{(6000-2000)}{6000 \times 2000}=\frac{1}{3000}$\\ & \lambda_3=3000 Å \end{aligned}$

questions.q: In Bohr's atomic model of hydrogen, let $K, P$ and $E$ are the kinetic energy, potential energy and total energy of the electron respectively. Choose the correct option when the electron undergoes transitions to a higher level :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total energy of electron is stated as& $E = - \dfrac{Z^{2}me^{4}}{8\left(nh{ε}_{0}\right)2}$, potential energy~$P = - \dfrac{Z^{2}me^{4}}{4\left(nh{ε}_{0}\right)2}$~and kinetic energy is given by~$K = \dfrac{Z^{2}me^{4}}{8\left(nh{ε}_{0}\right)2}$.

So, as electron makes transition to higher level, total energy and potential energy increases due to the negative sign while the kinetic energy of electron decreases.

questions.q: The electron in a hydrogen atom first jumps from the third excited state to the second excited state and subsequently to the first excited state. The ratio of the respective wavelengths& $\dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2}$ of the photons emitted in this process is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{4}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{R \times 7}{144}$
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{3}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{R \times 5}{36}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{1}}{{\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{R \times 5}{36} \times \dfrac{144}{R \times 7} = \dfrac{20}{7}$

questions.q: If ${λ}_{1}$ and ${λ}_{2}$ are the wavelengths of the third member of Lyman and first member of the Paschen series respectively, then the value of ${λ}_{1}: {λ}_{2}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda1} = R \left[\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{42}\right]

\dfrac{1}{\lambda2} =$R \left[\dfrac{1}{32} - \dfrac{1}{42}\right]$

$\dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2} = \left[\dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{16}\right]\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{16}\right] = \dfrac{7}{9 \times 15}$

$\dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2} = \dfrac{7}{135}$

$

questions.q: In a Frank - Hertz experiment, an electron of energy $5.6$ eV~passes through mercury vapour and emerges with an energy $0.7eV .$ The minimum wavelength of photons emitted by mercury atoms is close to:

questions.solution:
When electron pass through the mercury vapor, it losses some of its energy. The loss in $KE$ of electron $= \left(5 ⋅ 6 - 0.7\right)eV= 4.9eV$

$∴$ energy of radiation emitted $= 4.9eV$

$∴$ wavelength of radiation, $\lambda = \dfrac{1.24 \times {10}^{4}}{4.9}A \approx 250nm$

questions.q:
An electron of a hydrogen like atom, having $Z = 4$, jumps from ${4}^{th}$ energy state to ${2}^{nd}$ energy state, The energy released in this process, will be: (Given $Rch = 13 . 6eV$)

Where $R =$ Rydberg

constant $c =$Speed of light in vacuum

$h =$ Planck's constant
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Bohr's atomic theory, whenever an electron jumps from one orbit to another, there is always an emission or absorption energy in terms of emission or absorption of photons.

The formula to calculate the energy& \left(∆ E\right)$~of the emitted or absorbed photon when an electron jumps from a state with quantum number~${n}_{1}$~to another with quantum number~${n}_{2}$~is given by

$∆ E = - RchZ^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{{n}_{i}2} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{f}2}\right] . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$R$~is Rydberg's constant,~$h$~is Planck's constant,~$c$~is the speed of light and~$Z$~is the atomic number.

Substitute the values of the given parameters into~equation (1) to calculate the required energy.

$\begin{cases}∆ E & = & - 13 . 6 \times \left(4\right)2\left[\dfrac{1}{42} - \dfrac{1}{22}\right]eV \\ = & - 13 . 6 \times 16 \times \left[\dfrac{1}{16} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right]eV \\ = & 40 . 8eV\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A hydrogen atom in its ground state absorbs $10 . 2eV$ of energy. The angular momentum of electron of the hydrogen atom will increase by the value of~(Given, Planck's constant $= 6 . 6 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy absorbed is given by,

$\Delta E = 13 . 6 \times \left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right)$

$10 . 2 = 13 . 6 \times \left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right)$

Therefore, we get,~${n}_{1} = 1 \text{ and } {n}_{2} = 2$

The change in angular momentum

$\Delta L = \dfrac{{n}_{2}h}{2\pi} - \dfrac{{n}_{1}h}{2\pi} = \dfrac{h}{2\pi}$

$= 1 . 05 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$

questions.q: If $917Å$~ be the lowest wavelength of Lyman series then the lowest wavelength of Balmer series will be~$Å$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Rydberg's formula,

$\dfrac{1}{λ} = RZ^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{n^{2}1} - \dfrac{1}{n^{2}2}\right)

For the lowest wavelength in Lyman series,~${n}_{1} = 1, {n}_{2} = $\infty.

\dfrac{1}{λ} =$RZ^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{\infty 2}\right) =$RZ^{2}$

For Balmer series,~${n}_{1} = 2, {n}_{2} = $\infty

\dfrac{1}{\lambda '} =$RZ^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{22} - \dfrac{1}{\infty 2}\right) = \dfrac{RZ^{2}}{4}

So,

~\dfrac{1}{\lambda '} = \dfrac{1}{4\lambda}$⇒ \lambda ' = 4 $\times$917\overset{}{Å = 3668Å}$

$

questions.q:
A beam of monochromatic light is used to excite the electron in ${Li}^{+ +}$~from the first orbit to the third orbit. The wavelength of monochromatic light is found to be $x \times {10}^{- 10}m$. The value of $x$ is _____ .

[Given $hc = 1242eVnm$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy released in the transition will be,

$\Delta E = 13 . 6 \times Z^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{32}\right]= 13 . 6 \times {3}^{2} \times \dfrac{8}{9}eV = 108 . 8eV$

Now energy of photon can be written as,

$\dfrac{hc}{λ} = 108 . 8eV ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{12400}{108 . 8}\overset{o}{A} \approx 114\overset{o}{A}$

questions.q: A light of energy $12 . 75eV$ is incident on a hydrogen atom in its ground state. The atom absorbs the radiation and reaches to one of its excited states. The angular momentum of the atom in the excited state is $\dfrac{x}{\pi} \times {10}^{- 17}eVs$. The value of $x$ is ______ (use $h = 4 . 14 \times {10}^{– 15}eVs, c = 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{– 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the electron jumped to ${n}^{th}$ excited state.

In the ground state, energy $E = - 13 . 6eV$

So, using relation $12 . 75 = 13 . 6\left[\dfrac{1}{{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ 0 . 9375 = \left[1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right] ⇒ {n}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ n = \sqrt{16} = 4$

Now, angular momentum, $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{4h}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2h}{\pi}$

$= \dfrac{2}{\pi} \times 4 . 14 \times {10}^{- 15}$

$= \dfrac{828 \times {10}^{- 17}}{\pi}eVs$

Hence, the value of $x = 828$.
